capabilities: Automatically pull, commit, and push the vault to a Git remote in the background
Create symlinks that point AI tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf) at a vault AI-Brain folder
Edit AI system prompts, project rules, and coding standards in a visual manager
Scan outgoing commits for API keys and tokens and block matches
Create GitHub Issues from inside Obsidian
disambiguation: Not an AI agent itself; it manages Git sync and the configuration files of external AI coding tools.
extras: Manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. Requires Node.js fs and child_process permissions to run Git outside the sandbox. Secret scanning is heuristic, inbound sync is not scanned, and public-remote protection works only with github.com (no GitHub Enterprise); the README strongly recommends a private repository.
motivation: The README says it bridges the gap between local OS-level AI tools (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) and the Obsidian knowledge base.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in Git synchronization, and AI coding tool configs and prompts live outside the vault, scattered per machine and hard to share or back up.

relations.evidence: Create GitHub Issues directly from inside Obsidian without ever opening a browser.

requires.name: Git and a GitHub remote (GitHub CLI for issues)
At least one supported AI coding tool (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, etc.)

summary: Git-based vault sync plugin that manages AI agent system prompts and links local AI coding tools to the vault via symlinks.
